item.title: Bayelsa boat mishap death toll rises to 32, AIG visits scene
item.description: …Urges enforcement of life jacket, passenger capacity regulations By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa The Assistant Inspector-General of Police in charge of Zone 16, Regina Udoette, has visited Ayama-Ijaw waterside in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State following the boat mishap that claimed 32 lives. Udoette, who was accompanied by the Bayelsa State Commissioner of Police, Saka Ajao Adewale, visited the area on Monday to interact with marine transport workers and the Red Cross rescue team and receive updates on the ongoing search and recovery operation. During the visit, reports from the rescue site indicated that additional bodies had been recovered, raising the death toll from 29 to 32. The AIG commiserated with the Bayelsa State Government and residents over the tragedy, while commending President Bola Tinubu for his response and expression of sympathy following the incident. She expressed concern over alleged violations of maritime safety regulations, particularly the overloading of the vessel and failure to comply with life jacket requirements. According to her, the boat reportedly conveyed more than 500 passengers despite having a carrying capacity of 200. Udoette urged the state Ministry of Transport and marine unions to strengthen enforcement of safety regulations, particularly compulsory life jacket use and compliance with approved passenger limits. She also called for strict enforcement against operators who flout safety rules, stressing that passengers must take personal responsibility for their safety. Speaking with journalists, the AIG said she visited the waterside on behalf of the Inspector-General of Police to sympathise with the victims’ families and assess the situation. “I am here with my management team and the Bayelsa CP on behalf of the Inspector General of Police to sympathise with the people that died in the incident. I register our condolences and wish the injured quick recovery. “Besides, the maritime personnel told us of the refusal of passengers to obey safety rules, and the boat captain loaded over 500 persons for a boat with a 200-person capacity. That was a suicide mission and a disaster waiting to happen,” she said. Describing the deaths as avoidable, Udoette urged passengers and marine transport operators to comply with established safety regulations. “Some of these deaths are avoidable deaths. Many of the passengers refuse to obey safety rules. My Bible tells me obedience is better than sacrifice. There are rules and regulations on life jackets and overloading, but they refused. “For the living, this is a big lesson to everyone that wants to use a boat for their journey. They should listen to the rules. People should use common sense. This disaster is avoidable,” she added. The post Bayelsa boat mishap death toll rises to 32, AIG visits scene appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nigeria records 94% HIV viral suppression – NACA
item.description: The NACA director-general, however, identified gaps in HIV diagnosis, stressing the need to ensure more Nigerians know their status and access uninterrupted treatment. She said Early Infant Diagnosis coverage among HIV-exposed infants increased from 15 per cent in 2022 to 66 per cent in 2025. “While this is significant progress, we must do more to ensure that no child is left behind,” Ilori said. She said the 2026 World AIDS Day theme, “Ending AIDS Starts with Access: Equity, Ownership and Sustainability,” highlighted the need for equitable access to HIV prevention, testing, treatment and care. “Access must not depend on where you live, what you earn or who you are. It is a right, not a privilege,” she said. Ilori announced that NACA would unveil the National HIV Domestic Resource Mobilisation and Sustainability Strategy 2026–2030 on Dec. 1, as part of the World AIDS Day commemoration. According to her, the strategy will strengthen domestic financing, promote national ownership and sustain Nigeria’s HIV response amid declining global health funding. She also announced plans for a National Prevention Conference to explore innovative HIV prevention approaches, including self-testing, pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) and emerging prevention technologies. Dr Adebobola Bashorun, National Coordinator, National AIDS, Viral Hepatitis and STIs Control Programme (NASCP), said innovations would only save lives if they were accessible and affordable. “We can have the best technology and products, but without access they are useless,” he said. Bashorun said Nigeria was scaling up injectable HIV prevention medicines, oral PrEP and interventions to prevent mother-to-child transmission. UNAIDS Country Director, Ms Tina Boonto, said more than 1.5 million Nigerians living with HIV were accessing antiretroviral treatment. She, however, said Nigeria recorded about 64,000 new HIV infections annually, far above the fewer than 5,000 required to end AIDS as a public health threat. “Ending AIDS starts with ensuring everyone can access the services, medicines, technologies and information they need,” she said. Boonto called for increased HIV testing, expanded prevention services and stronger efforts to eliminate mother-to-child transmission. Dr Patrick Dakum, Executive Officer, Institute for Human Virology (IHVN), represented by the Director of Prevention, Care and Treatment, Dr Helen Omuh, stressed the need for equitable access to HIV services, community ownership and sustained domestic commitment. Dakum, speaking on behalf of implementing partners, reaffirmed their commitment to expanding effective interventions, strengthening domestic ownership and financing, and promoting sustainability. “We want to affirm that ending AIDS requires more than service availability. item.title: Four die as Omo-Agege survives alleged assassination attempt in Delta
item.description: By Efe Onodjae Former Deputy Senate President and Delta Central senatorial candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, has survived an alleged assassination attempt during a campaign tour of Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State. The attack, which occurred during a campaign visit, reportedly left four persons dead and four others critically injured. The Omo-Agege Campaign Organisation, in a statement by its Media Adviser, Sunny Areh, said armed men opened fire on the senator and his entourage at close range while he was addressing a crowd that had gathered to receive him. According to the organisation, Omo-Agege escaped being hit by bullets, which allegedly passed close to his head. It identified two of the deceased as its aides, Moses Anaughe and Akima Efemena Umukoro. The statement also named the injured as Chief Evance Ivwurie, Chuks Erhire, Tobore Agba and Ayodo Wanogho, adding that they were receiving medical attention. The organisation said eyewitnesses alleged that the attackers were heard shouting, “It’s Omo-Agege we want to kill,” describing the incident as a targeted assassination attempt rather than a political clash. However, a video obtained by Vanguard showed some NDC supporters lying bloodied on the floor of a hospital. When Vanguard contacted some eyewitnesses, one of them, Pius Eguono, said, “We were all shot in the crowd, but Efemena Umukoro has been killed. I’m on the run.” The post Four die as Omo-Agege survives alleged assassination attempt in Delta appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Tinubu, Sanwo-Olu court Igbo community ahead of 2027 polls
item.description: …Urge national cohesion, economic inclusion By Olasunkanmi Akoni President Bola Tinubu and Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, have urged Nigerians to rise above ethnic and regional divisions, emphasising the need for national cohesion, mutual understanding and inclusive economic development. The leaders made the call on Monday at the Ndigbo Lagos State Town Hall, organised by the Ndigbo National Dialogue and Development Initiative (NNDDI) at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, formerly the National Arts Theatre, Iganmu, Lagos. The engagement, attended by Igbo community leaders, business stakeholders and government officials, provided an opportunity to strengthen relations between the Igbo community and the Lagos and Federal Governments ahead of the 2027 general elections. Addressing participants, Tinubu urged Nigerians to embrace a shared national identity, irrespective of their ethnic, religious or regional backgrounds, saying the country’s development depended on the collective contributions of all citizens. He also stressed the importance of creating broad-based economic opportunities to enable Nigerians to contribute meaningfully to nation-building. “We must see ourselves as one people with a shared future. “Nigeria must rise above its divisions, because our true development depends on the active participation and commitment of every single citizen, regardless of background,” the President said. Earlier, Sanwo-Olu commended Tinubu for attending the gathering, describing his presence as an affirmation of the important role played by the Igbo community in the socioeconomic development of Lagos State. He acknowledged the contributions of Igbo political leaders, entrepreneurs, business associates and other stakeholders to the growth of the state. “The President’s presence here today is a significant gesture of recognition for Ndigbo and their rightful place in Lagos. “We deeply value the enduring contributions and longstanding partnerships of the political leaders, business associates, and stakeholders who continue to build this state alongside us,” the governor said. Reflecting on Nigeria’s democratic journey, particularly the political developments of 1999, 2003 and 2007, Sanwo-Olu also paid tribute to past and present leaders whose contributions helped shape the country’s political evolution. The town hall was designed to deepen engagement, address concerns affecting the Igbo community in Lagos and strengthen collaboration between community representatives and the two tiers of government. item.title: Obi Meets Niger State Residents, Urges Nigerians To Turn Out For 2027 Elections
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has urged Nigerians to turn out en masse for the 2027 general elections and remain at their polling units until their votes are counted and transmitted. Obi made the call during a campaign visit to Suleja, Niger State, where he urged voters to resist attempts to manipulate the outcome of the elections by ensuring that their votes were properly accounted for. He also criticised President Bola Tinubu, claiming that the president lacked the physical strength required to govern the country and was more interested in retaining power for personal gains than serving Nigerians. Obi, who is seeking the presidency for the second time, also promised to address Nigeria’s electricity challenges, pledging that his administration would generate, transmit and distribute at least 10,000 megawatts of electricity if elected. Niger residents gather for an engagement of NDC Presidential candidate Peter Obi. Photo: NigeriaNDCHQ/X He said Niger State would play a role in achieving the target, citing the state’s resources as part of the potential support for his proposed power-sector plan. The former Anambra State governor has been holding town hall meetings and engaging residents in different states ahead of the 2027 general elections. NDC Presidential candidate Peter Obi. Photo: NigeriaNDCHQ/X Obi contested the 2023 presidential election under the Labour Party, finishing third with 6,101,533 votes, behind Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, who polled 8,794,726 votes, and Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party, who received 6,984,520 votes. Tinubu is seeking re-election in 2027, while Obi is contesting under the NDC. Ahead of the election, major contenders include Tinubu under the APC, Atiku of the ADC, and Obi of the NDC. Other parties include the AAC, PDP, APM, SDP, PRP, Labour Party, and YPP. The presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for January 16, 2027, while the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections are slated for February 6, 2027. item.title: APC’ll win three South-East states; Obi will take Abia, Anambra — Bwala
item.description: The Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Policy Communication, Daniel Bwala, has projected that the All Progressives Congress will win three states in the South-East in the 2027 general elections, while conceding that Peter Obi could retain a stronghold in Abia and Anambra. Bwala made the projection during an interview on Channels Television’s Morning Brief on Monday, where he was asked how the ruling party intended to secure victories in the region. He said Obi’s popularity in the two states could make them difficult for the APC to win, but expressed confidence that the party would prevail in the remaining South-East states. “We will struggle in Abia. You see, in Abia and Anambra, Peter has a very convincing presence. Even in these two states, I am assuming that if we lose, we still come second, which is not a bad thing. Apart from these two states, the remainder of the states, we are winning,” Bwala said. The presidential aide, however, stressed that his assessment was a projection rather than a definitive prediction, noting that different political actors could arrive at varying conclusions from available data. He said the party was willing to acknowledge areas where it might face difficulties rather than make sweeping claims about its chances. “Where we think we may not, and I use the word advisedly because none of what I’m saying is cast in stone, right? It is projection, and two people from the same political party can have different projections based on our own interpretation of data,” he said. Bwala added that admitting potential weaknesses was more honest than claiming the APC would win everywhere, noting that his use of the word “struggle” referred specifically to the party’s chances of winning those states. The presidential adviser also expressed confidence in the APC’s overall prospects ahead of the 2027 elections, dismissing the opposition’s preparedness to challenge the ruling party. “I do not think the opposition is ready. Those who understand the political trajectory can see that they are already facing defeat,” he said. item.title: FG seeks 18-month completion period for new Carter Bridge
item.description: The Federal Government is seeking reduction in the period for construction of the new Carter Bridge. The Minister of Works, Sen. Dave Umahi, told the contractor handling the project, China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation (CCECC), to look at the possibility of reducing the time frame from 36 months to 18 months or 24 months. He said that the aim was to save more money and ensure that the new Carter Bridge would come on board before the existing one would go down. He said that CCECC had completed five per cent of the 1.9km bridge project without being paid any mobilisation fee. “No mobilisation fee has been paid to them, and the duration of this project is 36 months but I am striking a deal with their management, having seen that they have gone up to five per cent. “We are going to release, within this week, 30 per cent mobilisation fee to CCECC. “Another deal will probably be if we can reduce the construction period to about 18 months to 24 months; then, they can apply for loan so they can set up two other sections of piling. ” if they will do that, we are ready to give them a loan of 20 per cent so that they can set up, but they must give us APG – Advance Payment Guarantee,” the minister said. According to him, the Federal Government already has the APG for the 30 per cent mobilisation fee. “We are not allowed to pay more than 30 per cent but we can give a loan based on an agreement.” He emphasised that the bridge’s piling must be on a minimum of Schedule 60 thick steel pile. He said that the CCECC was meeting the specification. “We are very happy about that. We also directed that when they start their piling, we have to do a number of big lumps to protect the piles at the seabed,” Umahi said The post FG seeks 18-month completion period for new Carter Bridge appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Holding election with disputed voters’ register amounts to rigging – APM
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The Allied People’s Movement (APM) has warned that conducting the 2027 general elections with a disputed voters’ register would amount to rigging, accusing the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) of creating room for electoral manipulation by postponing its clean-up until after the polls. The party said the decision could undermine confidence in the electoral process, warning that unresolved concerns over the register could compromise the credibility of the 2027 elections. Responding to Vanguard’s enquiry on INEC’s decision, APM National Publicity Secretary, Abubakar Yusuf, described the postponement as another form of electoral manipulation and vowed that the party would resist any attempt to subvert the will of voters. “That’s another form of rigging the 2027 elections. Going into an election with a controversial register is tantamount to rigging, just like we had the case of electronic voting and BVAS,” Yusuf said. Citing the Kogi Central senatorial district election, Yusuf alleged that the experience showed how electoral outcomes could be manipulated in favour of the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC. “You remember in Kogi Central, election results were written by APC and the candidate declared as governor. I think that’s what they are going to adopt this time around,” he alleged. He insisted that APM would not accept any attempt to compromise the electoral process, declaring that the party would join other opposition groups to resist interference with voters’ choices. “APM will not succumb to INEC gimmicks. Any attempt to rig or tamper with the judgement of Nigerians in the forthcoming general elections will be resisted by not only APM, but opposition parties,” he said. Yusuf urged INEC to put its electoral preparations in order, warning against any action capable of compromising the 2027 elections. “INEC must do the needful by putting everything in order,” he added. item.title: Ghana defeat Morocco to win maiden Amputee Football World Cup title
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Ghana’s national amputee football team, the Black Challenge, have emerged champions of the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup after defeating Morocco 1-0 in the final held in Mexico. The victory marks Ghana’s first title in the competition and a historic achievement for the country’s football. The decisive goal came from a free-kick by Mubarik Mohammed, whose effort led to an own goal by Morocco, giving the Black Challenge the advantage they held until the final whistle. Mohammed also finished the tournament as its highest goalscorer, finding the net seven times during Ghana’s impressive campaign. The Black Challenge had earlier secured their place in the final after defeating defending champions Turkey on penalties in the semi-finals. They also recorded a 2-0 victory over Egypt to book their place in the last four. The triumph over Morocco brings Ghana’s successful campaign to a fitting end and earns the team its first world title in amputee football. item.title: Reps fault states over poor support for small businesses
item.description: …Propose N1bn monthly MSME fund per state, condemn high lending rates, red tape By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has faulted state governments for failing to adequately support small businesses despite increased federal allocations, proposing a minimum monthly intervention fund of N1bn in each state to boost Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). The Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, said state governments had the financial capacity to establish dedicated funds for entrepreneurs but had not demonstrated sufficient commitment to supporting grassroots economic development. Abbas, who spoke on Monday through the House Majority Leader, Prof. Julius Ihonvbere, at a stakeholders’ engagement organised by the House Committee on Small and Medium Enterprises in Abuja, said the survival of many small businesses depended largely on the resilience of their owners rather than meaningful government support. He argued that state and local governments must take greater responsibility for creating economic opportunities, stressing that the Federal Government alone could not address the country’s economic challenges. “There is no governor in this country that cannot put one billion a month in a special fund for MSMEs in his state. There is no state that cannot do it,” he said. The Speaker lamented that entrepreneurs who had managed to survive Nigeria’s difficult business environment were doing so largely without meaningful assistance from government institutions and intervention agencies. “Those that are surviving are surviving not because of government and agencies, but in spite of government and agencies,” Abbas said. He also criticised the bureaucratic procedures attached to accessing government intervention funds, arguing that excessive administrative requirements had undermined the effectiveness of programmes designed to support small businesses. “I’m a systems man, but I know this system is not working. And it will not work when you bureaucratise a procedure. A lot of red tape,” he said. Abbas further condemned high lending rates, warning that double-digit interest rates were inimical to the growth of small businesses. He said entrepreneurs needed affordable and flexible financing arrangements that would allow their businesses to stabilise and generate returns before repayment obligations became due. The Speaker urged state governors to establish transparent funding mechanisms, with effective monitoring and clearly defined eligibility criteria, to ensure that genuine entrepreneurs, particularly those operating at the grassroots, benefited from the proposed interventions. He also called on Nigerians to hold elected officials accountable at all levels, noting that the performance of state and local governments had direct implications for employment generation and economic prosperity. item.title: Sowore slams presidential candidates for leaving youths to fight electoral injustice
item.description: Human rights activist and former presidential candidate, Omoyele Sowore, has criticised opposition presidential hopefuls for allegedly leaving Nigerian youths to confront electoral injustice and repression while they position themselves to benefit from the outcome of the struggle. Sowore said politicians seeking to take advantage of demands for credible elections should also be willing to participate in protests and make sacrifices rather than leave the burden to ordinary Nigerians. In a post on X, he lamented that young Nigerians were expected to take to the streets and confront electoral manipulation while presidential candidates remained detached from the struggle. “Shame on presidential candidates who expect Nigerian youths to take to the streets, confront electoral injustice, endure repression, and make all the sacrifices, while they sit comfortably on the sidelines, waiting to reap the benefits of free and fair elections without lifting a finger!” he wrote. The activist made the remarks following his participation in a protest against electoral violence and manipulation at the headquarters of the Independent National Electoral Commission in Abuja. In an earlier post recounting the demonstration, Sowore said protesters chanted slogans demanding President Bola Tinubu’s removal as he arrived at the commission’s headquarters. He accused some opposition politicians of focusing on political negotiations and power-sharing arrangements instead of joining citizens to challenge what he described as electoral injustice. “While ordinary Nigerians confront the system on the streets, these politicians remain tucked away in cozy conference rooms, negotiating who gets what and who will control Nigeria’s resources if they eventually capture power,” he said. Sowore argued that political leaders should not expect to benefit from the sacrifices of citizens without contributing to the struggle for democratic accountability. “You cannot outsource the struggle for liberation and expect to inherit its rewards!” he declared. His comments come amid renewed political activities and debates over electoral credibility, political participation and opposition strategies ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: FIFA names UK as 2035 Women’s World Cup host
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland will jointly host the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup, while Costa Rica, Jamaica, Mexico and the United States will stage the 2031 tournament. According to Sky Sports, the UK bid was unopposed after FIFA declared it the only valid bid in April 2025. FIFA’s Congress ratified the bid on Monday, alongside the joint proposal from Costa Rica, Jamaica, Mexico and the US to host the 2031 competition. The 2035 tournament will be the first football World Cup held in the UK since the men’s competition in 1966. It is set to feature 48 teams and 104 matches over 39 days. FIFA has yet to confirm the dates or whether all four host nations will qualify automatically. The UK’s “All Together” bid proposed 19 stadiums across 15 cities: 14 in England, two in Scotland, two in Wales and one in Northern Ireland. Three additional venues — in Birmingham, Wrexham and a proposed new Chelsea stadium — could be added, taking the tournament to 22 stadiums across 16 cities. Presenting the UK bid, Sky Sports News presenter Jess Creighton said its ambition was to deliver “the most-watched FIFA Women’s World Cup ever”, predicting more than 3.5 billion viewers and over 4.5 million tickets sold. The 2031 edition will be the first Women’s World Cup contested by 48 teams. The four countries’ bid also ran unopposed before FIFA approved it. item.title: [PHOTOS] FG Targets December For Reopening Of Eko, Iddo Bridges
item.description: The Federal Government has assured Lagos residents that the Eko and Iddo bridges will be fully functional by December 2026, as rehabilitation and reconstruction works continue on the two critical transport links. The Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, gave the assurance during an inspection of the ongoing projects in Lagos, where he assessed the progress of work and commended the quality of interventions being carried out. This image shows ongoing reconstruction of the Iddo Bridge in Lagos. (Photo: Temitope Abe/Channels TV) At Eko Bridge, rehabilitation works were focused on addressing concerns surrounding some of its supporting structural components, while Iddo Bridge is undergoing reconstruction. Umahi expressed satisfaction with the progress recorded at both sites, assuring that the contractors would deliver the projects within the December deadline. “We are satisfied with what they’re doing. They are very fast in what they’re doing. They have good knowledge of what they are doing. And so we — as Ministry of Works — we are very satisfied,” the minister said. “And they promised us that by December, they will definitely complete the job and the full integrity of the bridge will be restored.” This image shows ongoing reconstruction of the Iddo Bridge in Lagos. (Photo: Temitope Abe/Channels TV) The inspection forms part of the Federal Government’s efforts to restore the two important infrastructure links, which serve thousands of commuters and businesses across Lagos. The ongoing construction activities have continued to affect movement around the affected corridors, with motorists and commuters having to contend with traffic disruptions. Umahi (2nd-left) commended the level of work done on the projects so far. (Photo: Temitope Abe/Channels TV) The minister’s assurance comes amid expectations that completing the projects will improve connectivity, ease traffic congestion, and enhance the safety of road users. Attention will now be on the contractors’ ability to meet the December deadline while ensuring that the restored infrastructure meets the required structural and safety standards.
